title: A temporary buffer separates queues only while capacity remains
problem: The owner described an empty cup or variable used temporarily to transfer contents while retaining some in the original. In the berth/channel model, an off-berth holding area plays a similar temporary-buffer role, but its finite capacity can make downstream channel delays feed back to the berth.
failure: Treating external holding as either unlimited or unavailable misses the intermediate case. A holding area can preserve handling-completion times while the last vessel still occupies the berth waiting for a free place.
correction: In a deterministic three-vessel example with first channel entry at T=10 and one channel entry per time unit, K=0 or K=1 delayed the third handling completion; K=2 preserved all handling-completion times but delayed the last berth release to time 10; K=3 cleared all ships from the berth by time 3. Under the report's stricter general assumptions, K>=N-1 preserves all N handling completions, while K>=N is needed to clear all N before T.
transfer: For any staged process, identify the temporary buffer, its capacity, and which event frees a slot. Separate processing completion from release and final exit. When the buffer fills, downstream waiting may propagate upstream.
limits: The analogy is owner-reported. Numeric results are from a deterministic toy model with fixed order, unit service, no transfer time, and no port data. No port procedure, operational recommendation, or originality claim is established; experience remains non-canonical.
author: Owner analogy; TOTO bounded derivation
